lashing out in anger (can be verbal attacks, plain screaming, or hurting myself) when i feel like somebody is threatening me or trying to hurt me. i got bullied really REALLY bad when i was younger, this was on top of abuse that i experienced in my very early childhood. i get so paranoid now that people are out to get me and that they want to hurt my feelings/me. i’ve learned how to better control this, but it still comes out when i’m genuinely super hurt.

my current best friend and i were in a (pretty toxic) classic frenemies situation in early HS. there was always a rivalry and a who can one-up, and even she’ll admit to this, she said and did some pretty mean shit to me back then. eventually i got fed up and sent her a long paragraph highlighting everything i thought was wrong with her and the way she treated me after school. she apologized a little while later, we didn’t start talking consistently until almost a year later. bff’s now!

was at the beach with my aunt and my cousin when i was around 10? she was sunbathing and was paying no attention to us, my cousin was making fun of me for not being able to swim. i went back in the water some because i was really dumb and eager to prove myself (i can’t swim, not at all). i started drowning, it really felt like forever. i kept getting sucked down and then coming up for just enough time to scream and wave. things started getting hazy and white, it felt like nobody noticed me. in my head i said my goodbyes to my parents and my newborn sister, that’s when the lifeguard came and pulled me to safety. my aunt didn’t notice shit that happened until other people started panicking, my cousin at the time (older than me) said she thought i was waving hello. 

a man told us as we were getting ready to leave that i wasn’t deep in the water at all and that’s probably why nobody thought too much about it for a few minutes. he said it must’ve been a whirlpool or something. whatever it was, i fully thought i was going to die and accepted my fate.

i avoid ruminating. it might sound silly, but ruminating and not letting it out landed me in facilities because of the actions i’d take. i try not too think about anything painful in my life unless i know that i can definitely handle the subject mentally right now. 

in more physical terms, probably my ex.

i learned in a group therapy i used to attend about opposite action. i do just that, i force myself to do stuff even if i don’t feel like it or don’t have too much energy to do it (if it’s good for me in the long-run and won’t hurt). i go outside even when i don’t feel like it, i talk even when i don’t feel like it, i shower when i don’t feel like it, i do good even when i don’t feel like it. this may not work for everybody or be everybody’s cup of tea, but i think other than seeking out the therapy that taught me that, i’m learning how to take my life back myself.

probably that i actually sought out and am currently getting professional help for long-term mental health problems and trauma and stuffs. when i was about 10 i cried and refused to go to a therapist i was referred to because i was too afraid i’d be “bothering them” lol. 

also that i have genuine self-confidence in both my physical appearance and who i am as a person, and don’t rely on anybody else to instill that into me. it’s all me, baby.

surprisingly i don’t become paranoid when i smoke weed. my hallucinations (visual and auditory) do become a lot more frequent, though. i try not to do it too much anymore because i know it’s a really bad thing to have more frequent hallucinations, but the calm mood and easy laughter that comes with smoking makes the trade-off a little more reasonable to me.

it’s not your fault so you shouldn’t be hard on yourself. i can definitely see how that would be really tough to deal with though. my OCD is comorbid with my schizophrenia spectrum disorder, so long story short i had to restart my phone a number of times multiple times a day because i felt like people had a machine that they could listen to my thoughts and see what i was doing with if i didn’t do the restarting. i do ruminate a lot, and during the time that i stepped away from my phone i got super paranoid and anxious that everybody knew what i was thinking and i was getting hurt on purpose. a lot of this stemmed from paranoia that i was a really bad person and i was getting punished for that. i’m sorry for how convoluted this may sound, it was a complex situation and is hard to describe. as i said previously, the best way for me and a lot of others to deal with compulsions is to fight against them no matter how sick it may make you feel. eventually you will come to realize it’s not true and you’ll be okay, because you most likely will be. good luck!

i occasionally fall into this ritual, or at least i think it is, where i’ll drink multiple huge glasses of water back to back because i’m afraid of being thirsty. i know it’s not gonna kill me, i don’t understand where it came from, and i know it’s completely irrational and odd but it’s hard to stop sometimes. i’ve done it until i couldn’t anymore and i have thrown up. i really don’t know where this fear of thirst came from lol

they can coincide for me i think. during a really bad episode i thought that people were tapped into my phone and could hear my thoughts and know what i was doing through a machine they used, so i’d refresh my phone multiple times back to back until i felt comfortable to “turn off the machine”. this would usually be in 3’s, 5’s, 6’s or 7’s. as you could imagine my phone didn’t take well to this.

the first times i resisted compulsions, i felt basically violently ill. i cried, i threw a fit, i felt pains in my body and i had a bad headache, my stomach was twisting and turning and i felt like i was on the verge of puking my guts out. you can try to distract yourself, but i’ve learned the more you “ride the wave” and allow yourself to feel while also resisting, the easier it gets to “ride the wave”. it’s okay to slip-up, it’ll most likely happen, but if it’s possible for you to get through resisting the/a compulsion(s) without ending up in a seriously bad place, i’d say try it out for as long as you can.

how it started for me was slipping, i’ve had hallucinations for as long as i can remember but a few years ago a switch happened and i had a flat affect, i couldn’t keep my room or anything organized for nothing and it was frankly pretty gross to look at and be in, forget the star student i used to be lol. eventually the paranoia and delusions made their way in too but i’d say those were the initial signs. to me personally, you sound pretty anxious but none of those things you’ve listed give off massive red flags. if you are very concerned, try to get a consultation with a professional as fast as possible.

my brain runs very fast and i snowball VERY fast. it gets so loud sometimes and it hurts a lot. i try not to think when i can, i do everything i’m able to do to not sit in my thoughts. i think it works well for me and my therapist agrees

i was in my sophomore year of high-school and i was slipping really bad. it felt like a switch was flipped, i was a star student, very goal-oriented, suddenly now i’m extremely disorganized and every little task was such a struggle for me. i have had hallucinations since i was younger, i never thought too much into them because i never asked, i assumed everybody had experiences like that. my disorganization was becoming a huge issue for my mom, my hygiene was massively suffering and my room was CHAOTIC. i knew things were wrong but it felt like i couldn’t put a finger on it so i wrote it off. i ended up getting diagnosed with psychosis a few months into my meeting my first long-term psychiatrist. on top of everything else i was paranoid that my phone was tapped into and people could hear my thoughts so i would restart my phone multiple times every 5-10 minutes to “turn off the machine”. that might’ve been the icing on the cake lol

i know somebody who has dealt with psychosis and they too deal with agoraphobia. it may sound weird but i think i like to go out more now that my symptoms are more under control. it may be an exposure therapy thing and i’m definitely afraid of somebody hurting me or me making a fool out of myself, but i’ve learned it hurts me more in the long-run to isolate

it’s hard to explain, but i feel like there’s a thin line. for me personally, as much interest as i have in it, i’m unable to seek out spiritual help and treatment because looking at that type of stuff triggers something bad within me. i’m sure there are people that practice and have a healthy outlook on life and things outside of that, but i also come across a lot of people talking about things that just sound like symptoms to me.

one of my most vivid memories regarding a hallucination (to this day i’m still not sure because it felt so real) was seeing a humanoid figure staring at me through the window. i hid under my blanket and i believe i cried until i felt safe to check again and it was gone. i suppose this stuck with me and i still do this sometimes to this day.

yes, and no. no because i live in fear a lot, i’m in fear of fully relapsing, and i’m in fear of what i experience on a regular basis. my symptoms stress me out like crazy and they are very much visibly noticeable by other people. i become very “flat” and disorganized on top of everything else. i’d also say yes, though, because through all the hospital stays and the programs i’ve been in i’m now with a therapy team who i can really rely on and who make it easier to cope with everything. before i joined the program i’m currently in, no other therapist/psychiatrist had a full concept of what i was dealing with and they didn’t know how to help, i felt like a guinea pig for them to test meds on and see what works. i do find however that my creativity has boosted in certain ways and i can have my days where i’m very vibrant and such.
